sanskrit_verse: अश्वस्थानाद् गजस्थानाद् वल्मीकात् संगमाद् ह्रदात् । मृत्तिकां रोचनां गन्धान् गुग्गुलुं चाप्सु निक्षिपेत् ॥
transliteration: aśvasthānād gajasthānād valmīkāt saṃgamād hradāt | mṛttikāṃ rocanāṃ gandhān gugguluṃ cāpsu nikṣipet ||
sph_interpretive_translation: From the resting place of horses, elephants, anthills, confluences, and lakes, one shall cast into water clay, rocanā, fragrances, and guggulu.
jurisprudential_principles: Causation arises through ritual alignment with elemental loci
Restoration logic demands removal of impurity at its source-point
Consciousness alignment necessitates material offerings in natural convergence zones
executable_legal_axioms: IF location_type IN [horse_resting_place, elephant_resting_place, anthill, confluence, lake] THEN action_required = TRUE

supreme_court_application: In adjudication involving environmental sanctity or territorial misconduct, the Court must recognize geospatial nodes as juridical instruments requiring conscious realignment rather than punitive zoning. Responsibility is determined by proximity to convergence points and capacity to restore elemental balance.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that misalignment manifests through disruption of elemental flow; anupūrvaśaḥ traces this back to improper engagement with convergence zones; proportional response entails ritual deposition, not penalty; reality remains non-punitive when correction aligns sensory experience with cosmic order.
